messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 - sudden spike in 5xx + gateway timeouts on inference-gateway (NA/EU) — error-rate 20% over 3m. Paging oncall. https://grafana.example/alerts/inf-gw-5xx-new

theo (oncall): I'm on. Seeing elevated 502/504 and some connect errors. Tagging @amaya @ryan for infra/runtime. Any recent LB/route changes pushed?

amaya: Just checked git history — there was an automated rollout 8m ago that changed the route weighting for /v1/embed to favor a new backend pool (pool-eu-fast). Also a new retry_policy was enabled in the gateway config (retries for 5xx + connect-failure, attempts=3).

ryan (eng-sre): Logs show repeated retries on same request ids, attempts 3, upstream frequently returning 503/504. Looks like the new pool has stricter limits and is tripping its circuit breaker, causing upstream 5xx responses that the gateway retries, amplifying load. Sample from proxy logs:

```
[2026-03-15T12:02:14Z] inf-gw pod/inf-gw-5 req=xyz attempts=3 route=/v1/embed upstream=pool-eu-fast status=504 msg="upstream request timed out"
[2026-03-15T12:02:15Z] lb frontdoor req=xyz attempts=2 downstream_status=502
```

amaya: Agreed. Mitigation plan: 1) temporarily turn off retries at edge to stop amplification, 2) reduce pool-eu-fast weight to 0% or drain it, 3) increase cluster circuit-breaker caps for pool-eu-fast, 4) scale pool-eu-fast horizontally if needed. I'll prepare the quick actions.

theo (oncall): Do the disable-retries then reduce weight. I'll coordinate the rollout. Doing kubectl patch to set attempts=0 on gateway config and then updating route weights.

```
# disable retries in configmap
kubectl patch cm inf-gw-config -n gateway --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/routes/0/retry_policy/num_retries","value":0}]'
# reduce canary weight
kubectl patch cm inf-gw-config -n gateway --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/routes/0/weighted_clusters/1/weight","value":0}]'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inf-gw -n gateway
```

incident-bot: Reminder: if errors do not fall below 10% within 10m escalate to eng-sre-incident and page secondary oncall.

ryan (eng-sre): Patches applied, pods restarted. Metrics show error rate falling from 20% -> 8% at +4m after restart. Latency also trending down. Good sign but we'll keep monitoring.

amaya: While retries were off, I patched cluster CB for pool-eu-fast to be more permissive as a temporary safety valve:

```
# temporary cluster cb bump via admin tool
infractl set-cluster-cb --cluster pool-eu-fast --max-conns 600 --max-pending 300
```

amaya: After CB bump + weight 0, errors dropped to ~2% and stable. No obvious customer data loss.

cs_lead: Notifying support rotation and product that EU customers may have seen failed /embed requests for about 10m window. Preparing a customer note: short outage window, transient errors mitigated. No SLA credit recommended yet pending PM review.

ryan (eng-sre): Follow-ups: revert the automated rollout that set high weight for pool-eu-fast until we can capacity-test it; add an automated guard that prevents route weight > 25% unless a canary pass metric is satisfied; add an alert for retry amplification (attempts per request > 1.4) to catch this earlier. I'll open INF-540 for postmortem.

theo (oncall): Handing off to @ryan for post-incident cleanup. I'm clear on pager. If anything spikes again, ping me. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT -> mitigated (status: recovering). Please document timeline and action items in incident runbook.

ryan (eng-sre): Saved snapshots, exported logs, and created a short-term playbook step to disable retries quickly. Scheduling a retro with runtime + infra tomorrow to discuss safer rollout controls and default retry policies.
